abstract: A generalized Nikulin surface is the K3 surface $F$ in the fixed locus of a symplectic involution on a manifold $X$ of $K3^{[2]}$-type; by Camere, Garbagnati, Kapustka and Kapustka, these are the K3 surfaces whose Néron–Severi lattice contains $E_7(-2)$ primitively, and the projective ones form $12$-dimensional families. We show that every projective generalized Nikulin surface $F$ admits an algebraic Hodge similarity of multiplier $2$ from a projective K3 surface $S_1$ of the same Picard number. The restriction from $H^2(X)$ to $H^2(F)$ kills the anti-invariant part and doubles the Beauville–Bogomolov form on the invariant part. The K3 surface $S_1$ is chosen with $T(S_1)$ rationally Hodge isometric to $T(X)$, and Markman's theorem makes this isometry algebraic on $S_1^{[2]} \times X$. When the endomorphism field of $T(F)$ is $\mathbb Q$, which holds for very general $F$, the surfaces $S_1$ and $F$ are not isogenous and the Hodge conjecture holds for $S_1 \times F$. For seven-nodal quartics the partner is a quartic surface with one singular point of type $E_7$. Nonsquare algebraic similarities from Nikulin involutions need Picard number at least $9$ and give families of dimension $11$; here the Picard number is $8$ and the families have dimension $12$. In the seven-nodal case the two transcendental lattices, of rank $14$, are even isometric as abstract quadratic spaces, so there only the Hodge structure forces the multiplier. For a finite group $G$ of symplectic automorphisms, the same argument with Hilbert schemes of $|G|$ points gives multiplier $|G|$ on families one dimension larger than quotients by $G$, for instance multiplier $3$ in dimension $8$ and $6$ in dimension $6$.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: Revision in response to the review of v1; the results are unchanged. (1) Supplement README: the d = 1..8 sweep in lattice_check.py is marked as exploratory, not a certificate. Its False column is explained: the trial lattices have determinant square class -2 against -1 for the K3 lattice, a parameter mismatch. The README now lists the expected outputs (included in expected/) and the software versions. (2) Abstract, Section 1 and Remark 4.1: the abstract rational isometry of the transcendental lattices is claimed only in the seven-nodal case. Even rank is necessary, not sufficient, because the Hasse invariants must also agree. (3) Proof of Theorem 1.3: in Markman's degree-reversing case the general-n correction is cup product by c_2^{n-1}, and the contributing component of Gamma has codimension 2n. (4) Remark 4.2 states j^*sigma != 0 before using it. Remark 4.4 now states the obstruction as a lattice-polarization bound (Hodge locus of dimension at most 13, rho(S_1) >= 7 on it), without identifying the Hodge locus with the locus of pairs (X, iota). (5) The restriction map is cited to [CGKK, Lemma 5.5, Section 5.2] and the rank 15 to [CGKK, Rem 5.6].
title: Generalized Nikulin surfaces and algebraic Hodge similarities of multiplier two
